transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-29
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Alex Torres (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Beacon Head of ML), Daniel Ortiz (Platform Eng), Ravi Patel (Security), Lena Vogel (Product), Speaker 1 (Beacon backup)

Summary: quick results walkthrough from last week's eval, decision on model commit candidates, discussion of emergency cutoff / graceful degrade behavior, next steps to validate rollbacks and run a tabletop drill. Notes: Beacon is leaning toward Dedicated for PII workflows but wants hosted fallback; security asks around KMS/HSM and audit logs remain blocking for final signoff.

Topics: 1) perf/cost numbers 2) model selection / pin strategy 3) fallback rules and emergency cutoff 4) security checklist 5) next steps and owner comms

[00:00:05] Jordan: alright everyone thanks for joining, I think we have full lane, quick roll call?
[00:00:12] Maya: hey, Maya here.
[00:00:13] Daniel: Daniel here.
[00:00:15] Ravi: Ravi.
[00:00:17] Lena: Lena.
[00:00:19] Priya: Priya from Redwood, Alex here too.
[00:00:25] Jordan: Cool. Quick agenda — Priya will walk through the bench numbers we did overnight, then we talk model commit (which variant to pin for the pilot), then fallback/emergency cutoff behavior and security asks.

[00:01:05] Priya: Great, I'll share my screen — disclaimer: these are internal quick sweeps, not the formal perf report but should be directionally accurate. We ran three families: v1.2 (baseline fp16), v1.3-quant (8-bit q*), and a trimmed v0.9 slim for low-latency. Workload is Beacon's 7-day sample (anonymized) with mixed short/long context, avg seq length ~420 tokens.

[00:02:12] Priya: Results — hosted (Redwood API) median p95 latency: v1.2 = 310ms, v1.3-quant = 240ms, v0.9-slim = 180ms. Token cost per 1k tokens: v1.2 = $0.95, v1.3-quant = $0.65, v0.9-slim = $0.40. Dedicated (reserved GPU) throughput for 8k batching: v1.2 = 18k tok/s, v1.3-quant = 26k tok/s. Note: these are with prefix cache enabled, we saw cache hits ~42% on the sample.

[00:03:05] Maya: ok that delta is bigger than we expected between fp16 and quant. How was accuracy — we can't loose core clinical QA.
[00:03:20] Priya: Good question. We ran the 200 canonical clinical prompts you sent. v1.3-quant drop in exact-match for structured extraction tasks was modest — from 94% to 92% on average; v0.9-slim dropped to 86% (and hallucination cases increased slightly). So quant is promising but slim is risky for our use.

[00:04:10] Daniel: curious on the KV cache impacts — in the raw logs I saw 'K V cash' flagged a bit, the transcrip — sorry, the traffic show some odd warm-up behavior. If cache hit is 42% can we expect that to improve in prod?

[00:04:35] Priya: Yes, cache hit should increase as warm prefixes stabilize. The sample includes lots of one-off patient notes which depress hit rate. For a patient portal with repeat templates we'd expect 55–70% hits. Also our runtime does continuous batching so cold-starts look worse in short windows.

[00:05:10] Jordan: So the ask from Beacon last week was: pick a commit candidate to pin for the pilot (we need to agree) and have a documented rollback/emergency cutoff path so product and ops know how to degrade. Thoughts?

[00:05:30] Lena: From product standpoint we want the highest accuracy that meets latency constraints. Our SLO is p95 < 350ms for live triage flows, and cost needs to land within 30% of current. Looks like v1.3-quant fits and slim is out.

[00:05:55] Ravi: Security input: if we go Dedicated for PII workloads we still need auditing and KMS integration; fallback to hosted is only acceptable if data is redacted or streamed encrypted. We cannot send raw patient identifiers to a hosted multi-tenant endpoint without HSM-backed envelope keys.

[00:06:30] Jordan: Good, so technical considerations: v1.3-quant seems like primary candidate. We'll propose pinning v1.3-quant with a soft-fallback to v1.2 (fp16) for safety, and an emergency cutoff that failsover to a rule-based stub response for critical endpoints if both model variants are unhealthy.

[00:07:05] Priya: To be explicit: commit policy option A — pin v1.3-quant as default route; route 5% shadow traffic to v1.2 for early detection; define error budget (5% increase in hallucination metric) to trigger rollback. Fallback paths: 1) auto-fallback to v1.2; 2) if latency/throughput breached, route to slim local lightweight model for non-PII flows; 3) emergency cutoff — return deterministic template with instruction to escalate to human.

[00:08:00] Maya: That seems reasonable. Two clarifying q's — what is the expected rollback RTO (how fast can we switch back) and how invasive is the rollback (does it require infra change)?

[00:08:18] Priya: Typical soft rollback within Redwood is a config flip in router — 30–90s to ramp if autoscaling not blocked. If we need to force cutover at region level or change Dedicated pool sizing it could be 5–10 minutes plus scaling time. We'll provide an escape hatch that is per-route and doesn't require infra redeploy.

[00:09:02] Daniel: Are we able to do canary evaluation metrics automatically? i.e. compare generation quality in the background and flag regressions without human review?

[00:09:18] Priya: Yes, we can integrate the eval harness. We can compute BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics for structured tasks, plus our hallucination detector. We recommend thresholding on both semantic matching and hallucination score. We'll ship a dashboard showing rolling two-hour windows.

[00:10:05] Jordan: On the security front — Ravi, can you summarize the must-haves for the pilot to be acceptable?

[00:10:15] Ravi: Sure: SOC2 report on file, SSO (SAML/Okta) for the Console, audit logs for model queries and admin actions retained 90 days (ideally 365), KMS integration for envelope keys and option for HSM for Dedicated, ability to set per-route data redaction, and an exportable compliance report. Also explicit data residency: EU-only for our EU cohorts.

[00:11:00] Alex: We have our SOC2 and ISO docs; I'll attach updated KMS integration notes. For HSM we have partners and can provide an architecture doc — will send today.

[00:11:20] Maya: Good. Back to model commit; can we get a short A/B plan — we want to measure real-world accuracy on a set of golden prompts before fully pinning.

[00:11:35] Priya: Proposal: 3-day canary at 10% traffic to v1.3-quant with shadowing to v1.2 for ground truth. We'll compute regressions on the canonical set and also watch live drift signals. If regressions cross threshold, auto rollback. We can instrument with webhook alerts to your Slack.

[00:12:10] Lena: Who owns the rollback trigger? Ops or Redwood? We need a runbook for people on-call.

[00:12:22] Jordan: We'll provide a runbook and recommend that Beacon's on-call owns the human approval for full rollback, but we'll implement the auto-fallback rules for immediate mitigation.

[00:12:40] Daniel: A quick infra question — when you say Dedicated pool, is that per-tenant GPU pool or shared with other customers? We need isolation and can't have noisy neighbors for some endpoints.

[00:12:55] Priya: Dedicated is per-customer GPU pool, isolated tenancy. You can configure multi-tenant within your own org if you want. There is also an option for private deployment (VPC) if you need network-level isolation / air-gapped.

[00:13:25] Ravi: For PII flows we want either Dedicated + KMS with HSM or Private deployment. Hosted fallback requires strong redaction or a pseudonymization step client-side.

[00:13:50] Priya: Noted. For the pilot we can route PII flows to Dedicated and non-PII to hosted until KMS is fully integrated. That reduces cost while meeting compliance.

[00:14:30] Jordan: Ok let's talk failure modes and emergency cutoff. Priya, can you describe typical thresholds and the safe behaviour?

[00:14:40] Priya: Sure. Error modes: 1) Increase in hallucination metric above threshold 2) sustained latency above SLO 3) spike in error rate or OOMs on model nodes. For (1) and (2) we recommend automatic downgrade to v1.2 for a rolling 5-minute window and alert. For (3) we recommend emergency cutoff that returns a deterministic JSON payload saying 'temporarily unavailable — please escalate to support' for critical endpoints and route traffic to a limited capacity queue to avoid cascading failures.

[00:15:40] Maya: That deterministic stub concerns product experience — will users see opaque errors?

[00:15:50] Jordan: The stub can be designed to be informative: return a short, human-friendly message and trigger an asynchronous follow-up to user via the application. Also we can implement a slow-path that enqueues request for later human review.

[00:16:20] Daniel: What about observability - we need token-level cost tracking and per-route latency breakdown in our SRE dashboard.

[00:16:30] Priya: Redwood Console exposes per-route token cost, per-model latency percentiles, tracing hooks you can pipe into Datadog or your ELK. We'll enable token attribution for QA so you can see top cost drivers.

[00:17:05] Lena: Back to the model pin: assuming we pick v1.3-quant, what's the plan to reduce drift during the pilot (model updates)?

[00:17:17] Priya: We recommend freezing the model version for the pilot. If necessary, we can do minor patch rollouts in a canary fashion and require explicit signoff for major architecture changes. We'll create a version-lock policy in your console.

[00:17:40] Ravi: On auditability — if a rollback happens, can we get an immutable record of requests/responses and the exact model binary/version used for future investigation?

[00:17:52] Priya: Yes, audit logs record model version, routing decisions, request id, and the censored payload as configured. You can set retention policies. For full forensic logs you should use Dedicated or Private with longer retention.

[00:18:20] Jordan: Quick interjection — competitors question: we heard Beacon's procurement is also evaluating Anthropic for guardrails; any concerns?

[00:18:30] Maya: They're on the list, but our main hang-ups are latency and cost — Anthropic looked strong on safety but pricier.

[00:18:45] Jordan: Ok. Let's make the commit decision explicit so we leave with an action. Options: A) Pin v1.3-quant as default with 10% canary and v1.2 shadow (recommended), B) Pin v1.2 fp16 as conservative default, C) Start with v0.9-slim for latency-critical features (not recommended for core clinical tasks). Which one do we want to agree on today?

[00:19:15] Maya: I'm inclined to A but want the canary thresholds spelled out and the rollback runbook before we flip.

[00:19:25] Lena: Agreed on A. Also need explicit performance budget and who triggers the full rollback.

[00:19:35] Ravi: Security says A is ok if Dedicated + KMS is in place for PII flows and we have the audit retention agreed.

[00:19:45] Jordan: So decision: go with Option A (v1.3-quant default, 10% canary, v1.2 shadow). Action: Priya to produce the canary thresholds doc and rollback runbook; Jordan to send invite for tabletop drill. Alex to share SOC/KMS notes. Beacon to provide final prompt set.

[00:20:20] Priya: One note — quant artifacts can behave differently for long sequences; we'll include sequence-length based gating so extremely long contexts (>2k tokens) route to v1.2 to be safe.

[00:20:40] Daniel: Good. On the canary eval, please include the hallucination delta and structured-extraction exact match as primary metrics.

[00:20:52] Priya: Noted. We'll add delta thresholds: hallucination +5% absolute triggers manual review; +10% triggers auto-fallback. Structured extraction drop >3% triggers manual review; >7% triggers rollback. We'll put numbers in writing.

[00:21:25] Maya: That helps. Now about cost — can we model monthly spend at 1M tokens/day across the mix?

[00:21:35] Jordan: Quick back-of-envelope: v1.3-quant hosted cost at $0.65/1k tokens -> for 1M tokens/day that's ~$650/day or ~$19.5k/month. Dedicated commit pricing can reduce unit cost but requires a monthly reserved commit. We'll send a pricing sketch.

[00:22:10] Lena: For budgeting, we'll need three scenarios: pilot, scale to 3M tokens/day, and a 99th percentile burst scenario.

[00:22:22] Jordan: We'll include that in the pricing sketch.

[00:22:35] Maya: Any open risks we should add to the runbook?

[00:22:45] Priya: I'll list: (1) quant regression on rare cases (2) cache warm-up causing p95 spikes (3) KMS integration delays (4) cross-region latency for EU cohort.

[00:23:00] Daniel: On cross-region, can we pin EU traffic to EU region?

[00:23:07] Priya: Yes, routing by region is supported; just ensure model variants are available in target region which we will confirm in the perf sweep.

[00:23:25] Jordan: We're at about halfway — any further customer questions?

[00:23:33] Ravi: One more compliance fine point — retention windows: we asked for 365 days; is that feasible for logs?

[00:23:42] Alex: For Dedicated we can stretch to 365, for Hosted there's an add-on. I'll document options.

[00:24:00] Maya: Ok. Priya, can you walk through the proposed rollback steps end-to-end? I want to make sure the people on-call can follow it.

[00:24:12] Priya: Sure — simplified runbook: detect (alert via metrics or manual), triage (check hallucination & latency dashboards), immediate mitigation (auto-fallback to v1.2 via routing flip), if degradation persists escalate to emergency cutoff (per-route stub) and open incident in PagerDuty, then postmortem and binary revert or re-quantize if needed. We'll attach exact CLI steps and console screenshots.

[00:25:02] Daniel: CLI steps are helpful. Also we need a 'test rollback' button we can click during theater drills.

[00:25:15] Jordan: We'll add a controlled rollback endpoint in the console for drills. It will require SSO admin approval.

[00:25:35] Priya: For verification we recommend a dry-run in staging where we flip traffic and monitor the traces.

[00:25:50] Maya: Sounds good. Let's schedule the tabletop drill — Jordan you said week of 10/5?

[00:25:58] Jordan: Yes, I'll send a 30-min slot and a pre-read.

[00:26:10] Lena: Can we get the perf sweep results before the drill?

[00:26:15] Priya: Yes, we'll deliver the sweep by 10/02. It will include region-specific numbers and cost modeling.

[00:26:30] Alex: I'll share SOC2 doc and a KMS/HSM note today.

[00:26:40] Ravi: And I'll confirm if 365-day retention is mandatory or negotiable for the pilot.

[00:26:55] Jordan: Any other blockers before we close?

[00:27:05] Maya: Just final ask: include a clear definition of 'hallucination' metric in the runbook so it's not ambiguous.

[00:27:15] Priya: Will do — we'll define detection heuristics and examples.

[00:27:25] Jordan: Great. Quick recap of decisions/action items so we leave with clarity.

Recap (auto notes):
- Decision: Pin v1.3-quant default, 10% canary, v1.2 shadow, sequence-length gating to route >2k tokens to v1.2.
- Rollback policy: auto-fallback thresholds (hallucination +10% auto rollback, latency SLO breach auto-downgrade), manual escalation to emergency cutoff.
- Security: Dedicated or Private for PII flows + KMS/HSM; Redwood to provide docs.
- Next: Priya perf sweep (due 10/02), Jordan to schedule tabletop (week of 10/05), Alex to share SOC/KMS notes (by 09/30), Beacon to provide final prompts (by 10/01).

[00:28:10] Speaker 1: thanks all.
[00:28:20] Jordan: Thanks folks. We'll follow up in email with attachments.
[00:28:30] Maya: thanks.
[00:28:35] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard product names (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache), speaker labels sometimes generic; content preserved as spoken incl. small filler words and interruptions.
